title: Price-Drop Claims on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
Where the identical itinerary in the identical fare brand of Air Ticket Fare Brands is publicly offered for less within the price-match window of the brand held, the difference is settled to the original form of payment up to the ceiling of that brand. The points below are answered from that term alone.

**Whether the offer found is a match at all.** The comparison is made against the brand's own public price on the same booking channel. A price found on a different channel is not a match, and a price found in a different fare brand is not a match.

**Whether the claim falls inside the window.** The window is measured from ticket issue and runs for the price-match window of the brand held. Worked on a hypothetical ticket issued at 14:20 on 4 March, under an illustrative window of 36 hours used only to carry the counting through: the window closes at 02:20 on 6 March, an offer found at 20:00 on 5 March falls inside it, and an offer found at 02:21 on 6 March falls outside it.

**Whether a brand that allows no cash settlement settles in some other form.** It does not. A brand that does not allow a cash settlement refuses the claim outright, and no voucher is offered in its place.

**What amount is settled.** The amount is the difference between what was paid and the lower public price, taken no higher than the ceiling of the brand held, and never more than the amount paid. Worked on hypothetical figures against an illustrative ceiling of 175.00 US dollars, a figure standing as the ceiling of no brand: a difference of 120.00 US dollars settles at 120.00 US dollars; a difference of 200.00 US dollars settles at 175.00 US dollars; and where the amount paid stands at 90.00 US dollars, the settlement is 90.00 US dollars.

**How many settlements a booking may receive.** The number of settlements made per booking is 1, however many drops occur, and a settled booking is not compared again.

**Which line the settlement is raised against.** The settlement is raised against the original base-fare line, and never against taxes, carrier fees or the agency booking service fee.

**A claim after the itinerary has changed.** A claim raised after the traveller has changed the itinerary is refused, because the itinerary compared is no longer the itinerary ticketed.
